papers.title: GeoEPred: A multimodal structure-aware geometric deep learning framework for Gram-negative bacterial secreted effector prediction with sequence semantics.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of effector proteins secreted by Gram-negative bacteria is important for elucidating bacterial pathogenic mechanisms and developing precise anti-infective strategies. Although existing methods have benefited from the strong sequence feature extraction capacity of pretrained protein language models, reliance on linear sequence information alone often fails to fully capture the three-dimensional conformational signals required for virulence functions. Meanwhile, conventional structure-based methods are limited by the scarcity of experimentally resolved protein structures. To
papers.summary: GeoEPred is a multimodal deep learning framework that combines protein language model sequence embeddings with predicted structural features to identify secreted effector proteins from Gram-negative bacteria. By integrating geometric structural signals with sequence semantics, it aims to overcome the limitations of sequence-only and structure-only prediction methods, which respectively miss conformational cues and suffer from sparse experimental structures.

papers.title: Molecular Evaluation of Deep Eutectic Solvents for Wet Algae Lipid Extraction and Biofuel Production.
papers.abstract: Microalgae represent promising feedstocks for biofuel production, yet cell-wall disruption remains a critical bottleneck for scaling up lipid extraction. This study evaluates four cholinium-based ionic liquids (ILs) and deep eutectic solvents (DESs) as green, energy-efficient pretreatment agents to facilitate the lipid release from Chlorella vulgaris under wet conditions. A geranic acid-based DES (CG 1-2 DES) was identified as the optimal agent, demonstrating direct wet biomass extraction with substantial process energy savings at comparable overall lipid yields. To minimize the energetic cost
papers.summary: This study evaluates four cholinium-based ionic liquids and deep eutectic solvents as pretreatment agents for extracting lipids from wet Chlorella vulgaris biomass, addressing the cell-wall disruption bottleneck in algal biofuel production. A geranic acid-based deep eutectic solvent (CG 1-2 DES) emerged as optimal, enabling direct wet biomass extraction with substantial energy savings at comparable lipid yields.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Discovery of Natural BACE1 Inhibitors with Enzymatic and Cellular Validation.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by excessive accumulation of β-amyloid (Aβ) peptides in the brain. Beta-secretase 1 (BACE1), the rate-limiting enzyme in the amyloidogenic processing pathway of amyloid precursor protein (APP), has been widely recognized as an important therapeutic target for reducing Aβ production. In the present study, nine machine learning-based predictive models for BACE1 inhibitors were constructed using Naïve Bayes (NB) and Recursive Partitioning (RP) algorithms. Subsequently, internal and external validations were conducte
papers.summary: This study built nine machine learning models (Naïve Bayes and Recursive Partitioning) to predict BACE1 inhibitors, a key enzyme target for reducing β-amyloid in Alzheimer's disease. The models were validated internally and externally, and top predicted natural compounds were confirmed through enzymatic and cellular assays. This demonstrates a practical ML-guided pipeline for discovering natural-product BACE1 inhibitors with experimental validation.

papers.title: Conformation- and Compound-Dependence of Ribose/2'-Deoxyribose Retention Patterns in Pyrimidine-Nucleoside Phosphorylase from Bacillus subtilis: A Four-Structure Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: In pyrimidine-nucleoside phosphorylase (PyNP), how the conformational state shapes substrate recognition remains poorly understood. In this study, all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) with MM-PB-(GB)-SA decomposition was performed on four structures of PyNP from Bacillus subtilis spanning the conformational range: the open 5OLN, the semi-open 5EP8orig, an energy-minimized contracted (closed-like) model 5EP8 min, and the cross-species closed-state crystal 1BRW, the last added to define the closed-state end. Thirteen structural probes were used (ten purine-like ribose/2'-deoxyribose analogues and th
papers.summary: This study uses all-atom molecular dynamics simulations with MM-PB(GB)SA energy decomposition to examine how different conformational states of Bacillus subtilis pyrimidine-nucleoside phosphorylase (PyNP) affect the retention of ribose versus 2'-deoxyribose in pyrimidine nucleoside substrates. By comparing four structures spanning open to closed conformations, the authors identify conformation- and compound-dependent patterns in sugar recognition. The work provides mechanistic insight into substrate discrimination in this enzyme family.

papers.title: Multiobjective Fluorescent Molecule Design with a Data-Physics Dual-Driven Generative Framework.
papers.abstract: Designing fluorescent small molecules requires simultaneous control over optical responses, brightness, and physicochemical constraints across vast, underexplored chemical spaces. Conventional generate-score-screen approaches become impractical under such realistic design specifications, owing to their low search efficiency, unreliable generalizability of machine-learning predictions, and the prohibitive cost of quantum chemical calculations. Here, we present LUMOS, a data- and physics-driven framework for inverse design of fluorescent molecules. LUMOS couples the generator and predictor withi
papers.summary: The authors present LUMOS, a generative framework that combines data-driven machine learning with physics-based quantum chemical calculations to inversely design fluorescent small molecules. It addresses the inefficiency of traditional generate-score-screen pipelines by jointly optimizing optical properties, brightness, and physicochemical constraints in a vast chemical space.

papers.title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Oxidation Resistance for Tertiary Phosphines Using Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potential-Aided Molecular Dynamics Simulation.
papers.abstract: Tertiary phosphines play important roles in a wide range of chemical reactions, but they suffer from oxidation in air. Here, we propose a computational workflow for the comprehensive prediction of oxidation resistance in tertiary phosphines based on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using Matlantis PFP, a universal machine learning interatomic potential (uMLIP). MD simulations were conducted for 51 different tertiary phosphines and analyzed to estimate mean survival time by survival analysis (τ). The resulting τ reproduced experimentally and theoretically recognized trends in oxidation resis
papers.summary: This paper introduces a computational workflow that uses a universal machine learning interatomic potential (Matlantis PFP) combined with molecular dynamics simulations to predict the oxidation resistance of tertiary phosphines. By simulating 51 different phosphines and applying survival analysis to estimate mean survival times, the approach reproduces known experimental and theoretical trends in oxidation resistance. This offers a scalable, simulation-based screening method for evaluating air stability of phosphine ligands.

papers.title: Bridging Visual Intuition and Chemical Expertise: A Virtual Collaborative Framework for Autonomous Nonadiabatic Dynamics Analysis.
papers.abstract: Analyzing nonadiabatic molecular dynamics trajectories traditionally heavily relies on expert intuition and visual pattern recognition, a process that is difficult to formalize. We present VisU, a vision-driven framework that leverages the complementary strengths of two state-of-the-art large language models (Doubao-Seed-1.6-Vision and DeepSeek-V3.2) to establish a "virtual research cooperation". This operates through a "Mentor-Engineer-Student" paradigm that mimics the collaborative intelligence of a professional chemistry laboratory. Within this ecosystem, the Mentor provides physical intuit
papers.summary: The authors present VisU, a vision-driven framework that combines two large language models (Doubao-Seed-1.6-Vision and DeepSeek-V3.2) in a 'Mentor-Engineer-Student' paradigm to autonomously analyze nonadiabatic molecular dynamics trajectories. The system mimics collaborative laboratory intelligence, using visual pattern recognition and chemical reasoning to interpret complex simulation data that traditionally requires expert intuition.

papers.title: Conformational Preference Classification of Integrin-Binding Ligands Using Free Energy Perturbation.
papers.abstract: Integrins are crucial cell adhesion receptors and attractive therapeutic targets, but developing safe small-molecule inhibitors has been challenging, at least in part due to inadvertent partial agonism caused by stabilization of the integrin's open, high-affinity state. To address this challenge, we present a computational approach using Absolute Binding Free Energy Perturbation (AB-FEP) calculations to predict whether a ligand will stabilize the open or closed integrin states, leveraging the difference between the ligand's binding free energy to the respective end states. Despite challenges p
papers.summary: This study presents a computational method using Absolute Binding Free Energy Perturbation (AB-FEP) to predict whether small-molecule ligands will stabilize the open (active) or closed (inactive) conformation of integrins. By comparing binding free energies to each conformational state, the approach aims to help design safer integrin inhibitors that avoid unintended partial agonism. The work addresses a key challenge in developing integrin-targeted therapeutics.

papers.title: Enhanced Sampling of Protein Conformations in AlphaFold3 with Repulsive Bias in the Diffusion Generative Model.
papers.abstract: Conformational changes in proteins are vital to their function yet remain challenging for state-of-the-art artificial intelligence, such as AlphaFold3 (AF3), to predict. It has been observed that AF3 sometimes fails to capture ligand-induced conformational changes, even though it explicitly includes ligand molecules that induce such changes. To address this challenge, we develop an enhanced sampling scheme that leverages the diffusion-based generative model used in AF3 to predict protein structures. Interpreting the diffusion generative model as a stochastic sampling process analogous to molec
papers.summary: The authors introduce an enhanced sampling method that adds a repulsive bias to AlphaFold3's diffusion generative model to better capture ligand-induced conformational changes in proteins. By treating the diffusion process as a stochastic sampler analogous to molecular dynamics, they improve AF3's ability to explore alternative protein conformations that it normally misses.

papers.title: Genome-wide-scale prediction of compound-protein interactions using foundation and language models based on three-dimensional structures of compounds and proteins.
papers.abstract: The identification of compound-protein interactions (CPIs) is crucial in the early stages of drug discovery. However, machine-learning (ML)-based methods based on one- and two-dimensional representations cannot capture important geometric information on the binding sites of CPIs, which limits their predictive accuracy.
papers.summary: This paper presents a machine-learning approach for predicting compound-protein interactions across the genome scale by leveraging foundation and language models that incorporate the three-dimensional structures of both compounds and proteins. The method aims to overcome the limitations of 1D and 2D representations, which fail to capture geometric binding-site information and thereby reduce predictive accuracy.

papers.title: Site-Specific Features Guiding Effective Reversible Photocontrol of Tryptophan Synthase With the Unnatural Amino Acid AzoF.
papers.abstract: This study delivers initial guidelines for the selection of effective incorporation positions for the azobenzene-based unnatural amino acid AzoF to facilitate the successful engineering of light-sensitive enzymes, dubbed photoxenases. Although photoxenases gain interest for the photocontrol of enzymatic activity across various fields their design has so far remained challenging. To ease particularly the selection of AzoF incorporation sites, we have systematically evaluated a total of 85 positions that differ in their biochemical and biophysical features in the bi-enzyme model system tryptopha
papers.journal: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates 85 different incorporation sites for the azobenzene-based unnatural amino acid AzoF in tryptophan synthase to identify features that enable effective reversible photocontrol of enzyme activity. The authors provide initial guidelines for selecting positions that yield light-sensitive 'photoxenases', addressing a key bottleneck in engineering photoswitchable enzymes.

papers.title: Predicting Enzyme Turnover Numbers and Enabling Rational Enzyme Evolution.
papers.abstract: Enzyme turnover number ( k cat  ) is a central kinetic parameter for biocatalysis, but experimental determination is low-throughput and existing computational methods inadequately model enzyme-reaction interplay. Here, we introduced MCKcat, a deep learning framework that integrates multi-scale convolutional feature extraction and cross-attention to enable deep, reciprocal fusion of enzyme sequence and reaction fingerprint representations for accurate k cat  prediction. We constructed MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset comprising 33 396 enzyme-reaction-based k cat  data points, covering both wild
papers.summary: The authors present MCKcat, a deep learning framework that combines multi-scale convolutional feature extraction with cross-attention to jointly model enzyme sequences and reaction fingerprints for predicting enzyme turnover numbers (kcat). They also built MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset of 33,396 enzyme-reaction kcat data points, and demonstrate its use for rational enzyme evolution. This addresses a key bottleneck in biocatalysis where experimental kcat measurement is low-throughput and existing computational methods poorly capture enzyme-reaction interplay.

papers.title: GPCR heteromers: Beyond the monomeric paradigm in neuropsychiatric drug discovery.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) constitute the largest druggable superfamily of membrane proteins and underlie approximately 35% of all approved medicines. Yet this conventional paradigm leaves a substantial minority of neuropsychiatric patients with incomplete efficacy, treatment resistance, or dose-limiting adverse effects. Converging evidence from structural biology, single-molecule biophysics, and molecular pharmacology has dismantled the monomeric model. GPCRs function in vivo as dynamic homomeric and heteromeric complexes in brain regions directly implicated in disease, including the
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This review argues that GPCRs operate in the brain as dynamic homomeric and heteromeric complexes rather than as isolated monomers, challenging the classical drug discovery paradigm. The authors synthesize evidence from structural biology, single-molecule biophysics, and pharmacology to suggest that targeting GPCR heteromers could improve treatments for neuropsychiatric disorders where current drugs show limited efficacy or dose-limiting side effects.

papers.title: A de novo GABPA Variant in a Patient with Multifocal Cutaneous Vascular Tumors of an Unclassified Entity.
papers.abstract: We investigated the genetic basis of a previously unclassified congenital vascular anomaly in a patient with multifocal cutaneous vascular tumors. Through genomic analysis, we identified a novel heterozygous de novo germline variant in GA-binding protein-alpha (GABPA), an ETS family transcription factor. Histopathologic evaluation demonstrated capillary-venous lesions lacking glucose transporter 1 expression, distinguishing this entity from common infantile hemangioma. Notably, the tumor vasculature exhibited a prominent alpha-SMA-positive perivascular cell layer, with nuclear localized GABPA
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study identifies a novel de novo germline variant in the GABPA transcription factor in a patient with multifocal cutaneous vascular tumors that do not fit any known classification. The tumors show distinct histopathology, including GLUT1-negative capillary-venous lesions and a prominent alpha-SMA-positive perivascular layer, suggesting GABPA dysfunction underlies this new vascular entity.

papers.title: Criteria-guided selection of alternative zinc-binding groups of HDAC3 inhibitors using in silico and in vitro approaches.
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are epigenetic enzymes linked to several biological functions and diseases. Class I HDACs (HDAC1-3) share high protein sequence and active site similarity. Hydroxamate-based inhibitors, while highly potent, are non-selective with poor pharmacokinetic profile, prompting exploration of alternative zinc-binding groups. The study applied criteria-guided identification of HDAC3 inhibitors with alternative zinc-binding groups following structure-based virtual screening, with a prioritisation of HDAC3-specific binding interactions and bidentate/monodentate interaction wit
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening to identify HDAC3 inhibitors with alternative zinc-binding groups, aiming to overcome the poor selectivity and pharmacokinetic issues of hydroxamate-based inhibitors. Candidate compounds were prioritized based on HDAC3-specific binding interactions and bidentate/monodentate zinc coordination, then validated in vitro.

papers.title: [Rational design for improving the thermostability of β-glucosidase from Bacillus thermoamylovorans].
papers.abstract: The β-glucosidase from Bacillus thermoamylovorans (Bgl52) has been identified as a thermophilic and acidophilic β-glucosidase, which constitutes the most critical component in the cellulolytic enzyme system for cellulose hydrolysis. Although Bgl52 is a thermophilic enzyme, its poor thermal stability at high temperatures restricts its long-term industrial application under elevated-temperature conditions. In this study, rational design strategies, including two free energy calculation programs (Fireprot and FoldX) and homologous sequence alignment, were integrated to perform single-point and mu
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study applies rational design strategies—combining free energy calculation tools (FireProt and FoldX) with homologous sequence alignment—to engineer the thermophilic β-glucosidase Bgl52 from Bacillus thermoamylovorans for improved thermal stability. The goal is to overcome the enzyme's poor stability at high temperatures, which currently limits its long-term industrial use in cellulose hydrolysis. The work demonstrates a computational protein engineering pipeline for enhancing enzyme thermostability.

papers.title: [Rational design and molecular engineering of a chitosanase for preparing specific chito-oligosaccharides with degree of polymerization≥5].
papers.abstract: To achieve efficient enzymatic preparation of specific high-degree-of-polymerization chito-oligosaccharides (degree of polymerization≥5, DP≥5), rational molecular engineering of chitosanase Csn46-Mut4 was performed in this study. Through site-directed mutagenesis coupled with DNS enzyme activity-HPLC product distribution screening, a superior mutant, C41A/T47A/V144A, was obtained. Under conditions of 55℃ and pH 5.5, the catalytic efficiency and thermostability of this enzyme were remarkably enhanced, reaching 2.56-fold and 1.67-fold those of Csn46-Mut4, respectively. Peak area normalization an
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study used rational design and site-directed mutagenesis to engineer a chitosanase (Csn46-Mut4) into a superior triple mutant (C41A/T47A/V144A) that produces chito-oligosaccharides with degree of polymerization ≥5 more efficiently. The mutant showed 2.56-fold higher catalytic efficiency and 1.67-fold improved thermostability, enabling better enzymatic preparation of these specific oligosaccharides.

papers.title: Site-specific phosphorylation of Ser352 drives aggregation of Tau R4 under acidosis conditions.
papers.abstract: In Alzheimer's disease, neurons undergo acidosis as their pH drops from ∼7.1 to ∼6.5. Here we elucidate the molecular mechanism of specific Tau aggregation only at this lower pH. We show that a specific phosphorylation event in the Tau R4 domain is coupled to this pH drop to drive a defined phase transition from condensates to fibrils. Using a combination of experimental and computational studies, our results demonstrate that site-specific phosphorylation of Ser352 is the molecular switch that induces aggregation of Tau only at the more acidic, disease-related pH. We designed and synthesized a
papers.summary: This study identifies phosphorylation of Ser352 in the Tau R4 domain as a molecular switch that triggers Tau aggregation specifically under the acidic conditions (pH ~6.5) found in Alzheimer's disease neurons. Combining experimental and computational approaches, the authors show this site-specific modification drives a phase transition from liquid condensates to fibrils, and they designed a synthetic peptide based on this mechanism.

papers.title: A water-pinning hotspot drives templated tau aggregation.
papers.abstract: Tau assembles into fibrillar aggregates that are pathological hallmarks of a group of neurodegenerative diseases collectively called tauopathies. Templated aggregation of naïve tau to seeding-competent fibrils that proceed from cell to cell is a key driver of prion-like progression of tauopathies. This study tests the hypothesis that tau, an intrinsically disordered protein (IDP), achieves in-register stacking to form seed-competent fibrils by a pinning action of tau to each other and/or the seed surface via a single dominant hotspot to avoid mismatch in tau stacking to fibrils. Structured sol
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how tau, an intrinsically disordered protein, forms seed-competent fibrils that propagate between cells in neurodegenerative tauopathies. The authors propose that a single dominant 'water-pinning' hotspot enables tau molecules to stack in register onto fibril surfaces, avoiding mismatched aggregation. This mechanism could explain the templated, prion-like spread of tau pathology.

papers.title: DesignMaster: A Multi-Conditional Diffusion Framework for Rational PROTAC Design.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable targeted protein degradation through ternary complex formation with E3 ubiquitin ligase. However, the rational design of PROTACs remains highly challenging due to limited structure-activity relationship data and the vast conformational diversity of linkers. Existing computational approaches can be broadly divided into structure-based ternary modelling methods and fragment-based linker generation models. Although these approaches have advanced PROTAC design, they typically neglect key physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during th
papers.summary: DesignMaster introduces a multi-conditional diffusion framework for the rational design of PROTACs, molecules that degrade target proteins by recruiting E3 ubiquitin ligases. Unlike prior structure-based or fragment-based methods, it incorporates physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during generation, addressing a key gap in computational PROTAC design.

papers.title: Targeting DYRK1A with rationally designed pyrazine-guanidine hybrids for Alzheimer's disease: design, synthesis, and biological evaluation.
papers.abstract: Dual-specificity tyrosine phosphorylation-regulated kinase 1A (DYRK1A) has been implicated in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) by regulating tau hyperphosphorylation and neuroinflammatory pathways, suggesting DYRK1A as an important therapeutic target. Herein, we report the rational design, synthesis and evaluation of a new class of low-molecular-weight pyrazine-guanidine molecular hybrids as potential DYRK1A inhibitors via an integrated computational and experimental approach. Molecular docking studies predicted good protein-ligand interactions, with compounds F1, F5, and F7 exhibi
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of novel pyrazine-guanidine hybrid molecules as potential inhibitors of DYRK1A, a kinase implicated in Alzheimer's disease through tau hyperphosphorylation and neuroinflammation. Using molecular docking followed by experimental evaluation, compounds F1, F5, and F7 showed promising protein-ligand interactions, suggesting these hybrids warrant further development as AD therapeutics.

papers.title: Sulfur source-driven global remodeling of gene expression in the fuel-biodesulfurizing Rhodococcus qingshengii IGTS8.
papers.abstract: Recent proteomics and metabolomics studies have confirmed the significance of understanding the fuel biodesulfurization phenotype at a global scale beyond the desulfurization 4S pathway. To reveal the transcriptomic adaptations in the model strain Rhodococcus qingshengii IGTS8 under biodesulfurization conditions, we conducted a time series comparative RNA-seq study using cultures of IGTS8 grown on either dibenzothiophene (DBT) or MgSO4 as the sulfur source. The RNA-seq data revealed many differentially expressed genes (DEGs) depending on the sulfur source and growth phase, and the strongest tr
papers.summary: This study used time-series RNA-seq to compare the transcriptome of Rhodococcus qingshengii IGTS8 grown with dibenzothiophene (DBT) versus MgSO4 as sulfur sources, revealing extensive sulfur-source-dependent and growth-phase-dependent changes in gene expression. The findings show that the biodesulfurization phenotype involves global remodeling of gene expression well beyond the canonical 4S desulfurization pathway.

papers.title: Evolutionary Dynamics-Aware De Novo Design of a Thermostable NS1-Derived Diagnostic Protein for Yellow Fever Virus.
papers.abstract: Serological diagnosis of neglected arboviruses remains hindered by extensive intra-genus cross-reactivity, compromising both assay specificity and epidemiological accuracy. In this study, we focused on yellow fever virus (YFV) as a model system to design and validate a generalizable de novo protein design framework integrating evolutionary genomics with structural modeling to rationally engineer diagnostic antigens with reduced cross-reactivity and improved cost-effectiveness. Through comprehensive evolutionary mapping over time of the YFV polyprotein, we identified conserved yet discriminator
papers.summary: The authors developed a de novo protein design framework that combines evolutionary genomics with structural modeling to engineer a thermostable diagnostic antigen derived from yellow fever virus NS1. By mapping the evolutionary dynamics of the YFV polyprotein, they identified conserved but discriminating regions to reduce cross-reactivity with related flaviviruses. This approach aims to improve serological diagnosis of neglected arboviruses.

papers.title: Mechanism-Driven Design of Metal-Phenolic Networks: From Precision Assembly to Multidimensional Synergistic Therapy for Brain Diseases.
papers.abstract: Background: Brain disorders, such as glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease and ischemic stroke, represent formidable challenges due to the highly restrictive blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the complex pathophysiological microenvironment, which severely compromise drug delivery and therapeutic outcomes. Metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), as a class of novel hybrid materials, hold great promise for overcoming brain delivery bottlenecks and enabling precise synergistic therapy by leveraging their unique physicochemical properties. However, a comprehensive synthesis of MPN designs tailored specifically to
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the design of metal-phenolic networks (MPNs) as drug delivery platforms for brain diseases like glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease, and ischemic stroke, focusing on how their physicochemical properties can overcome the blood-brain barrier. It emphasizes mechanism-driven engineering of MPNs for precision assembly and multidimensional synergistic therapy.

papers.title: Molecular glues: Recent advances in cereblon substrate identification and mechanistic insights.
papers.abstract: This highlight summarizes the recent advances in cereblon (CRBN) substrate discovery and mechanisms of action within the field of molecular glues. It emphasizes that molecular glue technology has transitioned from the stage of monofunctional targeted protein degradation to that of rational design and multidimensional regulation. Key recent breakthroughs include: (1) overcoming the limitations of canonical CRBN recognition motifs, identifying extensive novel substrates and unconventional recognition modes independent of fixed specific secondary structures; (2) reconceptualizing G protein-couple
papers.summary: This highlight reviews recent advances in understanding how molecular glues recruit the E3 ligase cereblon (CRBN) to degrade target proteins. It emphasizes a shift from monofunctional targeted protein degradation toward rational design and multidimensional regulation, including the discovery of novel CRBN substrates and unconventional recognition modes that do not depend on canonical motifs or fixed secondary structures.

papers.title: Pockets to products: a data-driven approach for classification of monoterpene synthases.
papers.abstract: Monoterpene synthases (mTSs) are a large family of enzymes, which have promising industrial applications, yet remain difficult to engineer due to complex and poorly understood sequence-function relationships. Here, we present a structure-based machine learning (ML) framework that accurately predicts whether a mTS is likely to produce linalool or limonene, chosen as canonical examples of linear and cyclic monoterpene products, respectively. Our approach identifies active site properties, which are used as ML features, enabling functional predictions that go beyond sequence alone. As residue pos
papers.summary: This paper develops a structure-based machine learning framework that predicts whether a monoterpene synthase enzyme will produce linalool (linear) or limonene (cyclic) by using active site properties as features rather than sequence alone. The approach addresses the difficulty of engineering these enzymes by capturing structure-function relationships that sequence-based methods miss.

papers.title: Morphology Evolution and Structural Reorganization of Enzyme-Biosurfactant Systems: Implications for Petroleum Interfacial Engineering.
papers.abstract: The escalating demand for sustainable chemical solutions in petroleum engineering has catalyzed the development of bio-based formulations characterized by high interfacial activity and low environmental toxicity. This study investigates the intermolecular interactions and structural evolution within composite systems comprising representative glycolipid biosurfactants and carbohydrate hydrolases. Rheological and light scattering assessments reveal that the introduction of enzymes triggers a transition from large-scale micelles to highly dispersed micro-aggregates, accompanied by a significant
papers.summary: This study examines how adding carbohydrate hydrolase enzymes to glycolipid biosurfactants changes the system's structure, causing a shift from large micelles to smaller, dispersed micro-aggregates. The findings suggest enzyme-biosurfactant combinations could improve interfacial performance for sustainable petroleum recovery applications.

papers.title: High-throughput physics-based enzyme engineering.
papers.abstract: Enzyme engineering aims to tailor natural enzymes for industrial and therapeutic applications, yet physically grounded rational design has been limited by a trade-off between accuracy and cost, leaving the field heavily dependent on expert intuition. Here we present a scalable physics-based framework that combines field-aware machine learning with molecular mechanics to capture enzyme electrostatics at quantum-mechanical accuracy while enabling efficient, atomistic exploration of reaction free-energy landscapes. Coupled with microkinetic modelling, the framework translates molecular free-energ
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint presents a scalable physics-based framework for enzyme engineering that combines field-aware machine learning with molecular mechanics to accurately model enzyme electrostatics and reaction free-energy landscapes. By coupling these calculations with microkinetic modeling, the approach enables high-throughput, atomistic exploration of enzyme variants, reducing reliance on expert intuition. The method aims to make rational enzyme design more accessible and efficient for industrial and therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Engineered mRNA nanostructures expand the design space of mRNA therapeutics through programmable protein expression and immune stimulation.
papers.abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have transformed vaccination and protein replacement strategies, yet efforts to improve their performance have focused largely on sequence engineering, nucleotide modification, and delivery vehicles. Here we show that mRNA function can be controlled by rational design of higher-order RNA architectures. We develop self-assembling mRNA origami (mRNA-OG), a class of unimolecular RNA nanostructures that encode protein-coding sequences within higher-order, programmable, and compact nucleic acid architectures. Using computational design and experimental validation,
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces mRNA origami (mRNA-OG), a class of self-assembling unimolecular RNA nanostructures that embed protein-coding sequences within programmable higher-order architectures. By rationally designing these structures rather than relying on sequence engineering or delivery vehicles alone, the authors show that mRNA function—including protein expression and immune stimulation—can be tuned through architectural design. This expands the design space for mRNA therapeutics beyond conventional sequence-level optimization.

papers.title: Protein eXplosion Imaging (PXI): Protein Structures from Laser-Driven Explosions.
papers.abstract: We investigate the structural information retained in the distribution of explosion ion trajectories from proteins subjected to strong ionization. Using molecular-dynamics simulations and machine-learning analysis benchmarked against an analytical approach, we show that low-resolution structural information can be retrieved from the explosion distributions alone. An ensemble of convolutional neural networks trained on simulated spherical ion maps recovers the radius of gyration and the three semi-axes of an ellipsoidal molecular envelope with prediction errors of 1.2 Å and 1.5 Å, respectively,
papers.summary: This paper proposes Protein eXplosion Imaging (PXI), a method that infers low-resolution protein structure from the ion trajectories produced when proteins are exploded by strong laser ionization. Using molecular dynamics simulations and convolutional neural networks trained on simulated spherical ion maps, the authors recover the radius of gyration and ellipsoidal envelope axes with errors of about 1.2–1.5 Å. The work suggests that explosion ion distributions retain usable structural information, offering a potential alternative route to low-resolution protein shape determination.

papers.title: KAN-GIN: Adaptive Nonlinear Molecular Representation Learning for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction supports virtual screening, lead optimization, and drug repurposing. This study investigates whether replacing the conventional post-aggregation multilayer perceptron within a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) transformation improves DTA prediction. Methods: The resulting KAN-GIN framework combines molecular-graph representations with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. It was evaluated on the DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline and representative
papers.summary: KAN-GIN replaces the standard multilayer perceptron in a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network transformation to improve drug-target affinity prediction. The framework combines molecular graph representations with a convolutional protein sequence encoder and was benchmarked on DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ against a matched GIN baseline. Results suggest that adaptive nonlinear transformations can enhance DTA prediction for virtual screening and lead optimization.

papers.title: Molecular Docking of Natural Products: Critical Appraisal of Current Methodology and Practical Guidelines.
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is among the most widely used techniques in structure-based drug discovery and has become integral to natural-product research. Despite substantial advances in computational algorithms and artificial intelligence, the methodological quality of published docking studies on natural compounds remains highly variable, and generally accepted methodological guidelines have yet to be established. This review critically evaluates current approaches to molecular docking of natural compounds, examines the specific features of different natural-product classes and protein targets, and o
papers.summary: This review critically assesses the current state of molecular docking studies applied to natural products, highlighting that methodological quality remains highly variable despite advances in algorithms and AI. It examines the specific challenges posed by different natural-product classes and protein targets, and proposes practical guidelines to improve rigor and reproducibility in this widely used structure-based drug discovery technique.

papers.title: Predicting Capsid Protein Binding Sites in Single-Stranded RNA Viruses Using Machine Learning from Local Geometric Features.
papers.abstract: Selective recognition of viral RNA by capsid proteins is essential for genome packaging during the assembly of single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) viruses. However, identification of capsid protein binding sites in the RNA genome remains challenging because current experimental techniques are labor-intensive and low-throughput, motivating the development of computational approaches. Here, we present a sequence-based framework that integrates RNA tertiary structural modeling, local geometric feature extraction, and machine learning to predict capsid protein binding sites. Using the Qβ bacteriophage as
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint presents a computational framework that combines RNA tertiary structure modeling, local geometric feature extraction, and machine learning to predict where capsid proteins bind within the genomes of single-stranded RNA viruses. Using the Qβ bacteriophage as a test case, the approach aims to overcome the labor-intensive, low-throughput nature of experimental binding site identification. The work suggests that sequence-derived structural geometry can serve as a practical predictor for viral genome packaging signals.

papers.title: Unveiling Novel Metalloprotease Inhibitors Targeting Botulinum Neurotoxin Through Structure-Based Virtual Screening of Drug Libraries and Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) is one of the most lethal biological substances to humans, which inhibits acetylcholine release by the presynaptic nerve in neuromuscular junctions. Of the existing BoNT serotypes, BoNT serotype A (BoNT/A) is particularly potent, making it the primary focus in neurotoxin research. Its catalytic domain exhibits similar structural features and zinc-dependent activity as thermolysin, a key bacterial enzyme, which provides a foundation for designing antibacterial agents targeting related protease mechanisms. Repurposing of preapproved drugs or existing medications has r
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening of existing drug libraries combined with molecular dynamics simulations to identify novel metalloprotease inhibitors targeting the catalytic domain of botulinum neurotoxin serotype A. The approach leverages the structural similarity between BoNT/A and thermolysin to repurpose preapproved drugs as potential therapeutics against this highly lethal neurotoxin.

papers.title: Deep Learning-based Modeling Enhances Efficacy of Natural Ligand CAR Binders Targeting CD70.
papers.abstract: CD70 is well-recognized as a promising "pan-cancer" chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell target. Prior work has shown that a "natural ligand" (NL)-based CAR targeting CD70, employing its physiological interaction partner CD27, may have therapeutic advantages over antibody- based CARs. Yet while antibody-based CARs are routinely optimized by affinity maturation of their scFv, whether the binding sequence of an NL CAR can be engineered to improve its function remains unexplored. Here, we combined deep learning with physics-based modeling to redesign residues at the CD27:CD70 interface, identif
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses deep learning combined with physics-based modeling to redesign the CD27:CD70 binding interface, aiming to improve natural ligand-based CAR T cells targeting CD70. The approach demonstrates that the binding sequence of a natural ligand CAR can be engineered to enhance its function, potentially offering a new optimization route beyond conventional antibody-based CAR affinity maturation.

papers.title: A multiscale modeling framework for transport of PEGylated lipid nanoparticle through the extracellular matrix.
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are one of the leading platforms for delivering nucleic acid therapeutics, yet their efficacy is limited by physicochemical interactions with the extracellular matrix (ECM) that trap the particles before they reach target cells. PEGylated nanoparticles mitigate these interactions by forming a protective steric layer on their surfaces. However, there is a lack of a predictive tool that gives mechanistic insights about how PEG surface density governs the underlying interaction and results in enhanced diffusive transport of LNPs through the ECM. Here, we present a multi
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint presents a multiscale modeling framework to predict how PEGylated lipid nanoparticles diffuse through the extracellular matrix, focusing on how PEG surface density controls particle-ECM interactions. The model aims to provide mechanistic insight into why PEGylation improves transport of nucleic acid therapeutics to target cells.

papers.title: Dibenzo[b,f]azocin-6(5H)-ones and Benzo[b]pyrido[2,3-f]azocin-5(6H)-ones: Useful Scaffolds for Development of Protein-Protein Interaction Inhibitors †.
papers.abstract: Modulation of protein-protein interactions (PPIs) by small molecules is a vital strategy in drug discovery. Nevertheless, due to the inherent nature of PPI interfaces, practical implementation of this approach remains a high-hanging fruit in medicinal chemistry. In this report, we develop a new line of PEX14-PEX5 PPI inhibitors by homologation of a previously developed dibenzo[b,e]azepin-6(6H)-one scaffold. The challenging chemistry of 8-membered ring formation led to the development of novel PEX14 inhibitors featuring a 6+8+6 tricyclic system. The obtained analogs were tested for their capabi
papers.summary: This paper describes the synthesis of novel dibenzo[b,f]azocin-6(5H)-one and benzo[b]pyrido[2,3-f]azocin-5(6H)-one scaffolds via challenging 8-membered ring formation, and their evaluation as inhibitors of the PEX14-PEX5 protein-protein interaction. The work expands the chemical space of PPI inhibitors by homologating a previously developed dibenzoazepinone scaffold, yielding compounds with a 6+8+6 tricyclic system that show potential for further optimization.

papers.title: Fast structural search for classification of gut bacterial mucin O-glycan degrading enzymes.
papers.abstract: The Enzyme Commission (EC) numbering scheme provides a hierarchical way to classify enzymes according to their catalytic functions. While recent protein language model (PLM) based approaches like CLEAN and ProteInter have improved sequence-based EC number prediction, they struggle with fine-grained classification at the deepest hierarchical level. Structure-based approaches for grouping similar proteins using alignment tools excel at finding proteins that share overall global structure, but suffer from high false positive rates when classifying proteins that are globally structurally similar b
papers.summary: The authors present a fast structural search method for classifying gut bacterial enzymes that degrade mucin O-glycans, addressing the difficulty of fine-grained EC number prediction at the deepest hierarchical level. Their approach improves on protein language model methods like CLEAN and ProteInter, which struggle with fine-grained classification, and on alignment-based structural tools that produce high false positive rates for globally similar proteins.

papers.title: Simulating Infrared Spectra of Matrix Isolation Experiments: What Works Best?
papers.abstract: Matrix isolation is an experimental technique which allows spectroscopists to observe highly reactive or weakly bound systems by trapping them in frozen noble gas matrices. In this work, we studied the viability of using ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) to simulate several H2S·amine complexes isolated in solid argon crystals, comparing the results with conventional density functional theory (DFT) harmonic and anharmonic calculations to assess the most practical and accurate method to calculate the vibrational spectrum of such systems. While AIMD accurately predicted the intensity ratios of
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks computational approaches for simulating infrared spectra of reactive or weakly bound molecules trapped in solid noble gas matrices, using H2S·amine complexes in argon as a test case. It compares ab initio molecular dynamics against conventional DFT harmonic and anharmonic calculations to determine which method best reproduces experimental matrix isolation spectra. AIMD was found to accurately predict intensity ratios, offering guidance on method selection for matrix isolation studies.

papers.title: Comprehensive insights into thermodynamic stability, optoelectronic properties, thermoelectric properties, and photocatalytic hydrogen evolution potential of halide double perovskites Rb2TlAlX6 (X = Cl, Br, I): first-principles and AIMD approach.
papers.abstract: Rubidium (Rb)-based halide double perovskites (HDPs) possessing tunable optoelectronic features have emerged as promising substances for optoelectronic, thermoelectric, and photocatalytic hydrogen production technologies. In the present work, Rb2TlAlX6 (X = Cl, Br, and I) HDPs are reported using a first-principles approach. The optimized lattice parameters, tolerance factors, and formation energy validate the cubic phase and thermal integrity of the studied HDPs at 300 K. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulation confirms thermal stability at 300 K, and phonon spectra validate dynamic sta
papers.summary: This study uses first-principles calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics to characterize the structural, thermodynamic, optoelectronic, and thermoelectric properties of rubidium-based halide double perovskites Rb2TlAlX6 (X = Cl, Br, I). The authors find that these materials are thermally and dynamically stable and show promising potential for photocatalytic hydrogen evolution, suggesting them as candidates for sustainable energy applications.

papers.title: A Multi-Scale Computational Framework for Anti-Persister Tuberculosis Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Latent tuberculosis (TB), caused by dormant, non-replicating Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), afflicts an estimated 1.7 billion individuals globally and remains a principal barrier to TB eradication. Dormant bacilli are phenotypically tolerant to conventional antibiotics and survive through continued dependence on oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and the electron transport chain (ETC), making bioenergetic enzymes, including the F1Fo-ATP synthase, cytochrome bcc:aa3 supercomplex, Type II NADH dehydrogenase (NDH-2) and cytochrome bd oxidase, compelling drug targets. This review proposes and r
papers.summary: This review proposes a multi-scale computational framework for discovering drugs that target dormant, drug-tolerant Mycobacterium tuberculosis persisters. It highlights bioenergetic enzymes like F1Fo-ATP synthase, cytochrome bcc:aa3 supercomplex, NDH-2, and cytochrome bd oxidase as promising targets for combating latent tuberculosis.

papers.title: Unraveling insights for ion transport enhancement by metal-organic framework-5 in polyethylene oxide and polyvinylidene fluoride electrolytes: classical molecular dynamics and metadynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: The structural and dynamical properties of simulation systems consisting of metal organic frameworks (MOFs), particularly MOF-5, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) salt, and two well-known polymers, poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) and poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO), in different compositions were investigated using classical molecular dynamics (cMD) and well-tempered metadynamics (WT-MD) simulations. The cMD simulations revealed that the PEO-based hybrid electrolyte system containing LiTFSI salt and MOF-5 (System D) exhibits the highest diffusion coefficient for Li+ ions and comp
papers.summary: This study uses classical molecular dynamics and well-tempered metadynamics simulations to investigate how MOF-5 affects lithium ion transport in polymer electrolytes based on PEO and PVDF. The PEO-based hybrid system with LiTFSI salt and MOF-5 showed the highest Li+ diffusion coefficient, suggesting that MOF-5 incorporation can enhance ion transport in solid polymer electrolytes.

papers.title: tris-Schiff Base Derivatives Containing Flurbiprofen as Potential Tyrosinase Inhibitors: Synthesis, In Vitro Evaluation, Molecular Docking, DFT and Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: A novel series of tris-Schiff bases of flurbiprofen has been synthesised via multi-step reactions, structures were deduced by means of HR-ESI-MS, 13C- and 1H-NMR spectroscopy and screened for their in vitro tyrosinase inhibitory potential. All the synthetic derivatives attributed noteworthy inhibition except compounds (11, 14 and 16), while eight compounds (5, 6, 7, 8, 19, 24, 22 and 18) were found potent comparing them with the standard kojic acid. Furthermore, the remaining nine compounds showed good to less inhibitory activity. A para-nitro containing compound 5 attributed the powerful tyro
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis of a new series of tris-Schiff base derivatives of flurbiprofen and evaluates their ability to inhibit tyrosinase, an enzyme relevant to melanin production and browning. Several compounds showed potent inhibition compared to the standard kojic acid, and molecular docking, DFT, and dynamics simulations were used to rationalize their binding and activity.

papers.title: Discovery and molecular insights of a novel pea-derived antioxidant peptide: From quantum chemical insights to oxidative stability of walnut oil.
papers.abstract: This study identified novel antioxidant peptides from defeasated pea protein and characterized their molecular properties and protective effects in a lipid system. Following ultrafiltration, Sephadex G-15 purification, Nano LC-MS/MS identification, and in silico screening, five unreported peptides (F1-F5) were selected for evaluation. Antioxidant activities varied across DPPH, ABTS, and hydroxyl radical assays, reflecting sequence- and assay-specific differences. Integrated experimental and computational analyses identified GIPYWTY (F1) as the lead peptide. Molecular docking revealed favorable
papers.summary: This study identified five novel antioxidant peptides from pea protein, with GIPYWTY (F1) emerging as the lead candidate through combined experimental and computational screening. The peptide showed protective effects against oxidation in walnut oil, suggesting potential as a natural food preservative.

papers.title: Fast and accurate construction of multiple sequence alignments from protein language embeddings with ARIES.
papers.abstract: Multiple sequence alignment (MSA) is a foundational task in computational biology, underpinning protein structure prediction, evolutionary analysis, and domain annotation. Traditional MSA algorithms rely on pairwise amino acid substitution matrices derived from conserved protein families. While effective for aligning closely related sequences, these scoring schemes struggle in the low-identity "twilight zone". Here, we present a new approach for constructing MSAs leveraging amino acid embeddings generated by protein language models (PLMs), which capture rich evolutionary and contextual informa
papers.summary: ARIES is a new method that builds multiple sequence alignments by using embeddings from protein language models instead of traditional amino acid substitution matrices. This allows it to align distantly related proteins in the low-identity 'twilight zone' more accurately and quickly than conventional MSA algorithms. The approach could improve downstream tasks like protein structure prediction and evolutionary analysis.

papers.title: Multidimensional molecular profiling reveals decidual and circulating NK cell dynamics in early and late pregnancy.
papers.abstract: Human pregnancy presents a unique physiological state that allows for growth of an antigenically dissimilar foetus. The immune system plays a key role in establishing and maintaining successful pregnancy, yet detailed understanding of immunological responses in pregnancy is lacking.
papers.summary: This study uses multidimensional molecular profiling to characterize natural killer (NK) cell populations in both decidual tissue and peripheral blood during early and late pregnancy. The findings reveal dynamic changes in NK cell composition and phenotype across gestation, offering a detailed map of immune adaptation during pregnancy. This work improves understanding of how the maternal immune system tolerates the semi-allogeneic fetus.

papers.title: State-dependent inhibition of LRRC8 volume-regulated anion channels by DCPIB.
papers.abstract: DCPIB is the prototypical inhibitor of leucine-rich repeat containing protein 8 volume-regulated anion channels (VRACs), yet the structural basis and state dependence of inhibition remain unclear. Here, we used chimeric channels, targeted mutagenesis, and electrophysiology to define the determinants of DCPIB inhibition and elucidate how drug binding is coupled to channel gating. Effective inhibition required coordinated contributions from extracellular loop 1 (EL1) and transmembrane domain 2 (TM2), which together form a functional module governing access to and stabilization of DCPIB-bound sta
papers.summary: This study identifies the structural determinants of DCPIB inhibition of LRRC8 volume-regulated anion channels, showing that extracellular loop 1 and transmembrane domain 2 together form a module controlling drug access and binding. Using chimeric channels, mutagenesis, and electrophysiology, the authors demonstrate that inhibition is state-dependent, coupling drug binding to channel gating. These findings clarify how a prototypical VRAC inhibitor works at the molecular level.

papers.title: Discovery of dietary polyphenols targeting the autoinducer-2 quorum sensing system of pathogenic bacteria.
papers.abstract: Targeting autoinducer-2 (AI-2) quorum sensing (QS) systems with dietary compounds represents a promising strategy to combat pathogens, yet mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we develop a machine learning-driven framework combining computational screening with multi-level experimental analysis to identify AI-2 quorum sensing interference molecules (QSIMs). A graph neural network (GNN)-based classifier (AI2IMpred) screens over 7000 phytochemicals and identifies dietary polyphenols as potent QSIMs. Using Salmonella Typhimurium LT2 as a model, we demonstrate that 17 polyphenols, including pterostilb
papers.summary: This study develops a machine learning framework (AI2IMpred, a graph neural network classifier) to screen over 7,000 phytochemicals for molecules that interfere with the autoinducer-2 (AI-2) quorum sensing system of pathogenic bacteria. Dietary polyphenols were identified as potent quorum sensing interference molecules, with 17 polyphenols validated experimentally in Salmonella Typhimurium LT2. The work highlights dietary compounds as potential anti-virulence agents targeting bacterial communication.

papers.title: Structure-guided discovery of novel ERα-binding peptides with in vitro antiproliferative activity.
papers.abstract: Uterine leiomyoma (UL) is an oestrogen-dependent tumour, and ERα is closely associated with abnormal proliferation of UL cells. This study used structure-guided virtual screening of a 59,319-member peptide library, followed by molecular docking, MST, MD simulation, MM/PBSA analysis, MTT assays, ERα knockdown, and RT-qPCR, to identify ERα-binding peptides. Four peptides showed ERα binding, among which Peptide-4 exhibited the lowest Kd value (9.3 ± 0.5 nM). Docking, MD simulation, and MM/PBSA analyses suggested a relatively stable ERα-Peptide-4 binding mode supported by hydrogen-bonding, hydroph
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This study used structure-guided virtual screening of a 59,319-member peptide library to identify novel peptides that bind ERα, the estrogen receptor implicated in uterine leiomyoma proliferation. Peptide-4 showed the strongest binding (Kd = 9.3 nM) and demonstrated antiproliferative activity in vitro, with molecular dynamics and MM/PBSA analyses supporting a stable binding mode. The findings suggest these peptides could serve as starting points for developing ERα-targeted therapeutics for estrogen-dependent tumors.

papers.title: Identification of Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 with potential relevance to prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Glutathione S-transferase Pi 1 (GSTP1) is frequently silenced in prostate adenocarcinoma (PRAD), yet whether its residual catalytic activity can be chemically enhanced is largely unexplored. Here, we identify Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 through structure-based screening, biophysical characterisation, and biochemical validation. Bio-layer interferometry (BLI) supported a concentration-dependent association between Crocin I and GSTP1, and enzymatic assays demonstrated enhanced catalytic activity. Michaelis-Menten kinetics showed that Crocin I increased Vmax without markedly alterin
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This study identifies Crocin I, a natural compound, as a positive modulator that binds to and enhances the catalytic activity of GSTP1, an enzyme often silenced in prostate cancer. Using structure-based screening, biophysical binding assays, and enzyme kinetics, the authors show Crocin I increases GSTP1 activity, suggesting a potential chemical strategy to boost residual GSTP1 function in prostate adenocarcinoma.

papers.title: Experimental Study on Anxiolytic and Antidepressant Effects of Zhi-Chi-Jie-Yu Granules in CUMS Mice and Prediction of Underlying Molecular Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the in‑vivo pharmacological effects of Zhi-Chi-Jie-Yu Granules(ZCK) on CUMS‑induced anxiety‑ and depression‑like behaviors in mice. Post‑hoc exploratory analyses including network pharmacology and molecular docking were further performed to generate potential mechanistic hypotheses for its anti‑depressant action.
papers.summary: This study tested a traditional Chinese medicine formula (Zhi-Chi-Jie-Yu Granules) in a chronic unpredictable mild stress mouse model and found it reduced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors. Network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses were then used to generate hypotheses about the molecular targets underlying these effects.

papers.title: Monomeric CRP is prevalent in the blood of patients with rheumatoid arthritis and correlates with clinically relevant markers.
papers.abstract: Elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) is a hallmark of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) flares. CRP exists as pentameric (pCRP) and monomeric (mCRP) isoforms with distinct functions, with pCRP generally pro-inflammatory and mCRP more immunomodulatory. Standard clinical assays do not distinguish between these forms, and it remains unclear whether elevated CRP in RA reflects structural variation. We investigated CRP isoform distribution and function in RA using biomolecular and biophysical approaches.
papers.summary: This study shows that monomeric CRP (mCRP), a distinct isoform from the standard pentameric CRP measured in clinics, is prevalent in the blood of rheumatoid arthritis patients and correlates with clinically relevant disease markers. Since standard CRP assays cannot distinguish between these isoforms, the findings suggest that isoform-specific measurement could improve how RA disease activity is assessed.

papers.title: Integrating network analysis and machine learning to explore the pharmacological targets and associations of oleanolic acid in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), a major type of non-small cell lung cancer, has high incidence and mortality rates. Oleanolic acid (OA), a natural pentacyclic triterpene compound, has demonstrated potential anti-tumor effects but its pharmacological effects in LUAD remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study combines network analysis and machine learning to identify potential pharmacological targets of oleanolic acid, a natural triterpene compound, in lung adenocarcinoma. The authors aim to clarify how this compound might exert anti-tumor effects in this common form of non-small cell lung cancer.

papers.title: Global research trends in tuberculosis drug-resistance mechanisms: a bibliometric and cross-database analysis.
papers.abstract: Drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) remains a major challenge to global tuberculosis control. In 2024, approximately 390,000 individuals developed multidrug- or rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB) worldwide, while treatment coverage remained limited to 42%, highlighting persistent gaps in DR-TB management. The mechanisms underlying DR-TB involve resistance-associated mutations, bacterial adaptation, host-pathogen interactions, and drug-target-related processes. A comprehensive evaluation of research trends is needed to clarify the evolution and future directions of this field.
papers.summary: This bibliometric and cross-database analysis maps global research trends on tuberculosis drug-resistance mechanisms, covering resistance-associated mutations, bacterial adaptation, host-pathogen interactions, and drug-target processes. It highlights persistent gaps in DR-TB management, noting that only 42% of the ~390,000 people who developed MDR/RR-TB in 2024 received treatment. The study aims to clarify the evolution and future directions of the field.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis prioritizes ALDH2 as a candidate Puerarin-associated target linked to macrophage infiltration in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Puerarin is a bioactive isoflavone with reported anti-tumor and immunomodulatory activities; however, its candidate molecular targets and associations with the immune microenvironment in lung adenocarcinoma(LUAD) remain incompletely defined. This study integrated computational analyses with a murine LUAD model to prioritize candidate puerarin-associated targets and evaluate their relationships with immune-cell changes.
papers.summary: This study combined computational multi-omics analyses with a mouse lung adenocarcinoma model to identify candidate molecular targets of the natural compound puerarin, prioritizing ALDH2 as a top hit. The authors further linked ALDH2 to macrophage infiltration in the tumor immune microenvironment, suggesting a possible immunomodulatory mechanism for puerarin in lung cancer.

papers.title: Identification of natural TLR4 modulators through network pharmacology and molecular modeling in SARS-CoV-2 Acinetobacter baumannii co-infection.
papers.abstract: Viral-bacterial co-infection with SARS-CoV-2 and Acinetobacter baumannii exacerbates hyperinflammation via Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)-mediated immune pathways. Using network pharmacology, an integrated protein-protein interaction network identified 30 key inter-species hubs comprising viral, bacterial, and human host proteins, with TLR4 achieving a high MCC score (722), highlighting its high topological centrality as a host immune target. Virtual screen of 2,820 natural compounds against the TLR4/MD-2 complex identified three top candidates, CID5898023, CID5403474, and CID74977829, with docki
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology to identify TLR4 as a central host immune hub in SARS-CoV-2 and Acinetobacter baumannii co-infection, then virtually screens 2,820 natural compounds against the TLR4/MD-2 complex. Three top candidates (CID5898023, CID5403474, CID74977829) were identified with favorable docking scores, suggesting potential natural modulators of TLR4-driven hyperinflammation.

papers.title: HIST1H2BJ is associated with poor prognosis and an immune-altered tumor microenvironment in glioma.
papers.abstract: Glioma, the most prevalent and aggressive primary malignant brain tumor, is associated with poor clinical outcomes. There is an urgent need for novel biomarkers to predict survival and therapeutic response, as existing markers offer limited prognostic utility.
papers.summary: This study identifies HIST1H2BJ, a histone gene, as a biomarker associated with poor prognosis in glioma patients. The authors also link its expression to an altered immune tumor microenvironment, suggesting it may influence how gliomas interact with the immune system. These findings point to HIST1H2BJ as a potential prognostic marker and therapeutic target in glioma.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic and single-cell analysis reveals a convergent cholangiocyte-associated host inflammatory program in biliary atresia and SARS-CoV-2-associated hepatobiliary injury.
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2-associated hepatobiliary injury and biliary atresia (BA) differ markedly in etiology and biological context, but both involve injury to the biliary epithelial compartment. Here, we performed integrative transcriptomic and single-cell analyses to investigate whether these distinct hepatobiliary injury contexts converge on a shared cholangiocyte-associated inflammatory host-response program. Bulk transcriptomic datasets from SARS-CoV-2-infected human liver organoids and BA liver tissues were integrated to identify shared transcriptional alterations, followed by functional enrichment,
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data from SARS-CoV-2-infected liver organoids and biliary atresia patient livers to test whether two very different biliary injuries converge on a shared cholangiocyte inflammatory program. The authors identify a common cholangiocyte-associated host inflammatory response signature, suggesting conserved injury mechanisms across distinct hepatobiliary diseases.

papers.title: Structure-based multi-pocket virtual screening identifies FDA-approved candidate compounds targeting MPXV thymidylate kinase.
papers.abstract: Mpox, caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), has emerged as a growing global health concern, yet effective targeted antiviral therapies remain limited. Thymidylate kinase (TMK), an essential enzyme required for viral DNA replication, represents a potential therapeutic target.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening against multiple pockets of the monkeypox virus thymidylate kinase (TMK) to identify FDA-approved compounds that could be repurposed as antivirals. The approach targets an essential viral DNA replication enzyme, offering a potential starting point for developing much-needed mpox therapeutics.

papers.title: Bioinspired and Biomimetic Nanocarriers: Advances in Exosomes and Cell-Membrane-Coated Systems for Therapeutic Applications.
papers.abstract: The translation of nanomedicine from bench to bedside has been thwarted by the limitations of conventional synthetic nanoparticles including rapid mononuclear phagocyte system (MPS) clearance, lack of target specificity, immunogenicity and poor intracellular delivery. To overcome these limitations, bioinspired and biomimetic nanocarriers are emerging as the next generation of therapeutic platforms. Bioinspired systems replicate the core biological design principles with engineered synthetic materials and biomimetic platforms use natural biological components such as cell membranes and extracel
papers.summary: This review discusses bioinspired and biomimetic nanocarriers, particularly exosomes and cell-membrane-coated systems, as next-generation therapeutic platforms that overcome limitations of conventional synthetic nanoparticles such as rapid clearance, poor targeting, and immunogenicity. It highlights how these systems replicate natural biological design principles to improve drug delivery and therapeutic efficacy.
